structured.answer: Joining is a no-brainer: on a 30,000 salary I put in 750 a month and the employer puts in 2,250. After 5 years the page says I'd have 136,457 ₪ in hand on 45,000 of my own money, and that's even after a scary −64,761 tax, which goes away if I just wait 6 years.

stuck.why: A huge minus right next to the result. It scared me until I saw the small chart: 'לפני 6 שנים: מס' / 'מ־6 שנים: פטור עד התקרה'. The default is set to 5 years, the one year where you get hit.
The calculator shows fees from 0.19% to 0.7%, and the cost table says 'עד 2% בשנה'. I guessed 2% is just the maximum allowed, but I'm not sure.

used: Heading 'מושכים את הכסף אחרי 5 שנים' and the small year chart labels
skipped: Grey notes under the chart (47% tax, 0.54% fee, inflation 2%)
unsure_meaning: hatched pink parts on the bars
מסלול מיטב השתלמות עוקב מדד S&P500 (13245)

findings.what: The calculator starts on 5 years, so the first result shows a big tax hit (−64,761). That makes joining look worse than it is, unless you notice the 6-year label.
Fees are 0.19–0.7% in the calculator but 'עד 2% בשנה' in the cost table. That's confusing; I can't tell what I'd really pay.
findings.where: Calculator line vs כמה זה עולה table

findings.what: Lots of small grey text under the chart that probably matters (tax 47%, ceiling 15,712), but nobody reads it.
Long dense text blocks before the calculator. On a phone I'd just scroll past them.
Some companies show up in one place and not another (מיטב, הראל, אלטשולר שחם), with no explanation
